title: client-semantic-rate-limits-and-tenant-fairness-protocol-2027
author: Priya Nandakumar
content:
Summary
=======
This document defines the Client Semantic Rate Limits (CSRL) protocol and a Tenant Fairness enforcement policy for Redwood inference endpoints. CSRL augments token- and request-level throttles with semantic quotas (by model, route, and customer intent) and a runtime fairness allocator so multi-tenant capacity is shared predictably during contention.

Goals
- Provide a clear API-facing contract for clients about what will be counted against quotas and when requests may be delayed or rejected.
- Ensure no tenant can monopolize shared serving capacity during bursts while preserving latency for high-SLO traffic.
- Allow operators to express weighted fairness, emergency overrides, and per-route cost signals.

Motivation
----------
Traditional rate limits (requests/sec, tokens/min) are necessary but insufficient for inference products because:
- Different request shapes have different cost/latency (short chat vs. long-generation).
- Customers need predictable degradation semantics for business-critical routes.
- Simple static quotas do not capture intent: e.g., many short low-cost requests should not be blocked by a few long heavy ones.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Redwood hosted inference endpoints and the shared Dedicated pools where multi-tenant scheduling is enabled. Not in scope: private on-prem deployments where customers control their own throttling (we provide the specification for interoperability).

Definitions
-----------
- semantic-unit: A normalized usage unit that expresses cost intent. By default: 1 request = 1 sem-unit for short calls; long generations translate to >1 sem-unit based on tokens and model profile.
- route: Logical API route (e.g., /v1/generate-chat, /v1/embed).
- tenant: Customer account namespace.
- weight: Configured numeric factor that biases fairness allocation (higher weight -> larger share under contention).

Protocol: how client semantics are communicated
-------------------------------------------
1) Client Hints (optional headers / body fields)
   - X-Redwood-Intent: "interactive" | "background" | "batch" (helps classify latency tolerance)
   - X-Redwood-Priority: numeric 0..10 (higher is more important; optional, used only if tenant permits)
   - model_hint: model id or model class (in request body) so router can apply model profiles

2) Server-side semantic costing
   - Cost computation: cost = ceil(max(1, (estimated_output_tokens + estimated_input_tokens) * model_cost_factor))
   - model_cost_factor is derived from the model capability manifest and per-variant profiler.
   - Example: short chat (est. 20 tokens, factor 0.2) -> cost = ceil(max(1, (20)*0.2)) = 4 sem-units.

3) Quotas and quotas buckets
   - Each tenant has: burst_bucket (tokens), sustained_window (quota per minute), route_caps (optional overrides), reserved_capacity (for Dedicated customers).
   - Semantic quotas are charged against the sustained_window and burst_bucket.

Fairness allocator (runtime behavior under contention)
----------------------------------------------------
1) Allocation inputs
   - available_capacity_sem_units (real-time view of runnable capacity)
   - active_tenants and their current queued demand (sem-units)
   - tenant_weights (configurable) and tenant_reserved_capacity
   - route_priority_modifiers (per-route SLOs)

2) Algorithm (high-level)
   - Compute fair_share = tenant_weight / sum(weights of active tenants) * available_capacity
   - Soft-saturate share for tenants whose queued demand is small: give them min(demand, fair_share)
   - If any tenant has reserved_capacity, subtract it from available_capacity before fair shares
   - Enforce per-tenant max concurrency and per-route SLO-preserving floor (e.g., preserve up to 10% of capacity for high-SLO routes)

3) Admission outcomes
   - admitted_immediately: enough capacity in fair share and burst_bucket
   - delayed_with_handover: request enqueued with an ETA and client receives Retry-After + queue token
   - rejected_quota_exceeded: 429 with reason and suggested mitigation (reduce tokens, switch model)

Enforcement points and contract messages
---------------------------------------
- Edge Gateway: lightweight pre-checks for basic token and sustained_window allowance; returns immediate 429s for obvious quota violations.
- Router/Admission Coordinator: authoritative semantic-cost computation, fairness allocation, queue tokens.
- Runtime Executor: final admission, precise local eviction when kernel preemption occurs.

Client-visible response headers and bodies
- X-Redwood-Semantic-Cost: integer sem-units charged
- X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: sem-units remaining in sustained_window
- Retry-After: seconds if delayed
- body: {"error": "quota_exceeded", "suggestions": ["reduce_max_tokens", "use-compact-model"]} 

Configuration examples (table)
----------------------------
| tenant_tier | sustained_quota_per_min | burst_bucket | default_weight | reserved_capacity |
| enterprise  | 10000                   | 5000         | 10             | 30%               |
| startup     | 2000                    | 500          | 2              | 0%                |
| free        | 200                     | 50           | 1              | 0%                |

Example JSON quota policy (declarative)
```
{
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "sustained_quota_per_min": "5000",
  "burst_bucket": "1200",
  "default_weight": "5",
  "route_overrides": {
    "/v1/generate-chat": {"weight": "8", "floor_capacity_pct": "10"}
  }
}
```

Operational guidance and observability
-------------------------------------
- Metrics to emit (per-tenant and cluster-aggregated):
  - csrl.request_cost (count sem-units charged)
  - csrl.queue_length (requests queued)
  - csrl.admissions.{immediate,delayed,rejected} (counts)
  - csrl.fair_share_fraction (ratio of allocated to theoretical fair share)
- Dashboards: per-tenant heatmap (sustained_quota vs consumption), global contention tracer, and top-10 route-actions causing the most semantic cost.
- Alerts:
  - P1 if global utilization > 92% and queued requests for >5 minutes
  - P2 if any enterprise tenant sees >2% rejected rate for >30m

SLOs (example baselines)
- Admission latency for interactive intent: 95th percentile < 120ms when cluster utilization < 80%
- Queue ETA accuracy: median error < 200ms

Rollout and migration plan
-------------------------
1) Canary (2 weeks): enable semantic costing and allocator in read-only mode for 5% of traffic (emit metrics but do not enforce).
2) Soft-enforce (4 weeks): activate enforcement for low-risk tenants (internal, dev, free tier) with advisory 429s (include mitigation suggestions).
3) Enforce-by-default: enable strict enforcement for shared pools with full observability and automated incident escalation.

- Migration checklist:
  1. Populate model_cost_factor from profiling jobs (eng-serving-runtime).
  2. Backfill tenant weights from billing / contract data (billing team).
  3. Add client-gradual-notice emails and SDK warnings (devx).

Safety and overrides
-------------------
- Emergency throttle: SRE can mark a tenant as emergency_exempt for X minutes (audited action).
- Graceful degradation: if capacity drops, the allocator reduces batch sizes and preserves high-SLO route floors before reducing interactive allocations.

Tracing and auditability
-----------------------
- Every admission decision must attach a trace id and a reason: {"admit":true, "reason":"fair_share"}. This is stored in short-term audit logs for 7 days and long-term cost accounting for 90 days.

Ownership and review cadence
---------------------------
- Owner: eng-platform (oncall: inference-routing-team)
- Reviewers: capacity-planning, billing, devx, security
- Review cadence: quarterly for config defaults, immediate review for any changes to weight or reserved_capacity affecting enterprise tiers.

Appendix A: Client SDK best practices
------------------------------------
1) Surface X-Redwood-Intent via SDK helpers; prefer enum values rather than free text.
2) On 429 with "quota_exceeded" prefer: exponential backoff with jitter, optionally switch to a smaller model.
3) Include optional estimate fields in request to help server cost estimation: {"estimated_output_tokens": 64}.

Appendix B: Sample observability query (pseudo):
- sum by (tenant) (rate(csrl.request_cost[5m])) / sum(rate(csrl.admissions.immediate[5m]))
